A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Omni-DPO study. The main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–H support reliable comparison, including matching content across table relocations and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original textual, mathematical and multimodal experiments, along with ablations, gradient-stability analyses and generated-response case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and D.4–D.8, Figures 4–6 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The quality and performance weights, length normalization, calibrated NLL objective and Algorithm 1 procedure are retained. Renaming NLL comments to c-NLL does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same textual, mathematical and multimodal coverage, including UltraFeedback, NuminaMath and MM-RLHF Image data. The multimodal experiments highlighted in v2's contribution list already appear in v1's appendices.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including DPO, SimPO, the v0.2 comparisons, and the RAFT and iterative-DPO comparisons in Table D.5.

E3.justification: Training settings, data selection, evaluation metrics, decoding procedures and model configurations are retained. Reformatting and relocating Tables C.1 and C.3 preserves their parameter values and model assignments.

E4.justification: The existing gradient-stability analysis in Figure 5b receives a small revision to the stabilized gradient trace. The question tested and qualitative finding remain unchanged, as do the other ablations, sensitivity analyses, overfitting analyses and case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose seed 42, single-run mathematical pass@1 evaluation, and the same standard-error and 95% confidence-interval reporting in Table D.8. No additional runs or new uncertainty procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Figure 5b slightly lowers an early stabilized-gradient peak from approximately 25.6 to 25.3, beyond merely rescaling the axes. Benchmark and ablation tables, scaling scores and Appendix G responses remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives and gradient derivations in Sections 2–3 and Appendices B and E are retained. Equation changes concern typesetting rather than mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly includes multimodal tasks in the contribution list, and the conclusion adds a training-efficiency benefit. These modestly broaden the main claims without changing the central dual-perspective optimization contribution.

C2.justification: The explanations of quality–difficulty mismatch, overfitting, gradient weighting and c-NLL calibration are retained. Data-quality dependence, limited multimodal model scale and remaining calibration questions receive the same substantive qualifications.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code and models from 'will be available' to 'are available' at the same repository. This changes reported resource availability; implementation, hardware and data-processing details otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds five references concerning hallucination mitigation, VisionThink, MedAgent-Pro, SurgRAW and RoboMamba to the multimodal/RLHF discussion. The positioning relative to DPO and iterative preference optimization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammatical and terminology edits, adds precise appendix pointers, clarifies radar-plot descriptions, and updates affiliations and contact information. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 5b's axes are rescaled, Figure 6 receives clearer labels, larger legends and revised colors, and several captions are refined. Training tables are reformatted, while Tables C.3 and D.6 are relocated; no new figure or table is introduced.

improvement.justification: Clearer plot labels and legends, better-organized training tables and more precise appendix pointers modestly improve readability. v2 also reports code and models as available. These are limited documentation and reproducibility gains; the method, benchmark evidence and substantive limitations remain largely unchanged.
